description: 100 questions on OOP inheritance (coding and logic based, intermediate/advanced level)

questions.question: How do you define a class Dog that inherits from Animal?
What does a child class inherit from its parent?
questions.answer: All methods and class/instance attribute access (attributes themselves live on the instance)

questions.question: class Animal: def speak(self): return '...'; class Dog(Animal): pass. What does Dog().speak() return?
class Animal: x = 5; class Dog(Animal): pass. What does Dog.x return?
What does isinstance(Dog(), Animal) return for class Dog(Animal)?
questions.answer: True (a child instance is an instance of the parent)

questions.question: class Dog(Animal): pass. What does isinstance(Dog(), Dog) return?
a = Animal(); what does isinstance(a, Dog) return?
questions.answer: False (a parent object is not an instance of the child)

questions.question: What does type(Dog()) == Animal return?
questions.answer: False (type checks the exact class, not parents)

questions.question: What does issubclass(Dog, Animal) return for class Dog(Animal)?
What does issubclass(Animal, Dog) return?
What does issubclass(Dog, Dog) return?
questions.answer: True (a class is a subclass of itself)

questions.question: class A: pass; class B(A): pass; class C(B): pass. What does issubclass(C, A) return?
What does isinstance(C(), A) return for class C(B) and B(A)?
class A: pass; class B(A): pass. What is B.__mro__?
class Base: pass; class Child(Base): pass. What does Child.__bases__ return?
class A: def m(self): return 'A'. class B(A): pass. What does B().m() return?
class A: def m(self): return 'A'. class B(A): def m(self): return 'B'. What does B().m() return?
class A: def m(self): return 'A'. class B(A): def m(self): return super().m() + 'B'. What does B().m() return?
What does super() allow a child method to do?
questions.answer: Call the parent version of a method (or the next class in the MRO)

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self): self.x = 1. class B(A): pass. What does B().x return?
class A: def __init__(self): self.x = 1. class B(A): def __init__(self): self.x = 2. What does B().x return?
class A: def __init__(self): self.x = 1. class B(A): def __init__(self): super().__init__(); self.x += 10. What does B().x return?
class A: def __init__(self, n): self.n = n. class B(A): def __init__(self, n, m): super().__init__(n); self.m = m. What does B(1, 2).m return?
class A: def __init__(self): self.n = 0. class B(A): def __init__(self): pass. What does B().n raise?
questions.answer: AttributeError (the parent initializer was never called)

questions.question: Does a child inherit the parent's __str__ if it defines none?
questions.answer: Yes, special methods are inherited too

questions.question: class A: def __str__(self): return 'A'. class B(A): pass. What does str(B()) return?
class A: def m(self): return 'parent'; def call(self): return self.m(). class B(A): def m(self): return 'child'. What does B().call() return?
questions.answer: 'child' (parent code dispatches to the child's override)

questions.question: What name describes the behavior where a base-class method calls an overridden method?
class A: def __init__(self): self.x = 1. class B(A): def __init__(self): super().__init__(); self.y = 2. What does B().__dict__ contain?
class A: x = 1. class B(A): pass. b = B(); print(b.x) outputs?
class A: x = 1. class B(A): x = 2. What does B.x return?
class A: x = 1. class B(A): x = 100. print(A().x, B().x) outputs?
What lookup order is used for obj.attr on a child instance?
questions.answer: Instance dict, then the MRO: child, parents, grandparents, ..., object

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self): self.v = 'A'. class B(A): def __init__(self): super().__init__(); self.v = 'B'. What does B().v return?
Can you call a grandparent method with super().super()?
questions.answer: No, super() only goes to the next class in the MRO; chain it via each class or use the MRO

questions.question: class A: pass. class B(A): pass. What does A.__subclasses__() return?
questions.answer: A list of direct subclasses, e.g., [<class 'B'>]

questions.question: What does isinstance(obj, (A, B)) return if obj is an instance of B and B extends A?
questions.answer: True (isinstance accepts a tuple of classes)

questions.question: What does issubclass(B, (A, C)) do?
questions.answer: True if B is a subclass of any class in the tuple

questions.question: class A: def m(self): return 'A'. class B: def m(self): return 'B'. class C(A, B): pass. What does C().m() return?
class A: pass. class B: pass. class C(A, B): pass. What is C.__mro__?
class A: pass; class B(A): pass; class C(A): pass; class D(B, C): pass. Is this inheritance valid?
questions.answer: Yes, it is the classic diamond and works via C3 linearization

questions.question: In a diamond D(B, C) with both B and C extending A, how many times does A.__init__ run via super()?
questions.answer: Once (the cooperative MRO calls each initializer exactly once)

questions.question: class A: pass. class B(A): pass. class C(A): pass. class D(B, C): pass. What is super().somemethod() able to find in D?
questions.answer: The next class in D's MRO after the class defining the call

questions.question: Can a child class use a method the parents don't define?
questions.answer: No, calling it raises AttributeError unless some ancestor defines it

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self): self._x = 1. class B(A): def get(self): return self._x. What does B().get() return?
class A: def __init__(self): self.__x = 1. class B(A): def get(self): return self.__x. What does B().get() raise?
questions.answer: AttributeError: '__x' is mangled to '_B__x' in B, but the parent stored '_A__x'

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self): self.__x = 1. def get(self): return self.__x. What does A().get() return?
questions.answer: 1 (inside A, __x is mangled to _A__x which exists)

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self): self.__x = 1. class B(A): def __init__(self): super().__init__(); self.__x = 2. How many private slots does a B instance have?
What does b._A__x return for a B instance from the previous setup?
Can a child access a parent's name-mangled attribute directly like b.__x?
questions.answer: No, b.__x is looked up as _B__x and not found

questions.question: class A: def hi(self): return 'hi'. class B(A): pass. print(hasattr(B(), 'hi')) outputs?
What does getattr(Dog(), 'sound', 'none') return when Animal has sound?
class A: pass. class B(A): pass. How do you test whether B is a subclass of A at runtime?
How do you list all classes B inherits from?
class A: def f(self): return 1. class B(A): def f(self): return super().f() + 1. class C(B): def f(self): return super().f() + 1. What does C().f() return?
questions.answer: 3 (chain: 1 from A, +1 in B, +1 in C)

questions.question: class A: def f(self): return 1. class B(A): def f(self): return super().f() + 1. What does B().f() return?
What does super() return in Python 3 inside a class method?
questions.answer: A proxy object that delegates calls to the next class in the MRO

questions.question: Can super() be used inside a classmethod with cls?
questions.answer: Yes, super().classmethod(...) works, forwarding to the next class

questions.question: class A: n = 0; @classmethod def bump(cls): cls.n += 1. class B(A): pass. What does B.bump() increment?
class A: n = 0; @classmethod def bump(cls): cls.n += 1. class B(A): pass. B.bump(); B.bump(); print(A.n) outputs?
class A: n = 0; @classmethod def bump(cls): cls.n += 1. class B(A): pass. B.bump(); print(B.n, A.n) outputs?
class A: def m(self): return 'A'. class B(A): def m(self): return 'B'. b = B(). What does type(b).m(b) return?
class A: def __init__(self): self.x = 'A'. class B(A): def __init__(self): self.x = 'B'; super().__init__(). What does B().x return?
class Animal: def speak(self): return '...'. class Dog(Animal): def speak(self): return 'woof'. items = [Dog(), Animal()]. What does [i.speak() for i in items] return?
class Animal: def describe(self): return self.speak(). class Dog(Animal): def speak(self): return 'bark'. What does Dog().describe() return?
Can a child class inherit from two unrelated classes simultaneously?
class A: x = 1. class B: x = 2. class C(A, B): pass. What does C.x return?
class A: x = 1. class B: x = 2. class C(B, A): pass. What does C.x return?
What is C3 linearization used for?
questions.answer: Computing the MRO that respects base order and avoids inconsistent hierarchies

questions.question: class A: pass. class B(A, A): pass. What does it do?
questions.answer: Raises TypeError (a base class cannot appear twice in the same class definition)

questions.question: How do you call the parent constructor when the parent needs arguments?
class Parent: def __init__(self, name): self.name = name. class Child(Parent): def __init__(self, name, age): super().__init__(name); self.age = age. What does Child('A', 3).name return?
What does Child.__dict__ contain that Parent.__dict__ doesn't (for the setup above)?
questions.answer: Child's own __init__ (and its docstring entry), while Parent keeps its own __init__

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self, *args, **kw): print('A'). class B(A): def __init__(self): print('B'); super().__init__(). What gets printed by B()?
class A: def __repr__(self): return 'A()'. class B(A): pass. print(repr(B())) outputs?
What happens if neither the child nor parent defines a method you call?
questions.answer: AttributeError propagates, then object base is checked and fails

questions.question: class A: def m(self): return 1. class B(A): pass. class C(B): def m(self): return super().m() * 10. What does C().m() return?
What does isinstance(C(), A) return in that setup?
How do you make a class MY class a subclass of list, dict, etc.?
class L(list): pass. l = L([1,2]); l.append(3); print(len(l)) outputs?
class D(dict): def keys(self): return list(super().keys()) + ['extra']. What does D(a=1).keys() return?
class A: def __len__(self): return 3. class B(A): pass. print(len(B())) outputs?
class A: def __iter__(self): return iter([1, 2]). class B(A): pass. print(list(B())) outputs?
What is the benefit of inheritance over copying parent code?
questions.answer: Code reuse, consistent interface, and polymorphic behavior

questions.question: class A: def m(self): return 'A'. class B(A): def m(self): return super().m(). What does B().m() return?
What does `object` mean at the top of every MRO?
questions.answer: It's the ultimate base class all Python classes inherit from

questions.question: Is issubclass(A, object) true for any class A?
questions.answer: Yes, object is the root of the class hierarchy

questions.question: class A: pass. class B(A): pass. class C(A): pass. class D(B, C): pass. Is D an instance-compatible parent of B?
questions.answer: No, D is a child of B, not a parent

questions.question: What does isinstance(D(), B) return in that diamond?
class A: pass. class B(A): pass. What does issubclass(A, B) return?
questions.answer: False (only the child is a subclass of the parent)

questions.question: Can a base class use an attribute only defined by the child?
questions.answer: Yes, if accessed via self during a child instance's method call (dynamic dispatch); otherwise it may AttributeError

questions.question: class A: def info(self): return self.species. class B(A): species = 'dog'. What does B().info() return?
class A: def info(self): return self.species. What does A().info() raise?
class A: def f(self): return 'A'. class B(A): def f(self): return 'B'. class C(B): def f(self): return super().f() + 'C'. What does C().f() return?
What is the purpose of super().__init__() with no extra arguments?
questions.answer: To run the parent's initialization (setting inherited attributes) in cooperative inheritance

questions.question: class A: def __init__(self, **kw): self.a = kw.get('a', 1). class B(A): def __init__(self, **kw): super().__init__(**kw). What does B(a=99).a return?
Does inheritance copy methods into the child's __dict__?
questions.answer: No, inherited methods are found via the MRO, not copied

questions.question: class A: def m(self): return 'A'. class B(A): pass. print('m' in B.__dict__) outputs?
class A: def m(self): return 'A'. class B(A): pass. print('m' in dir(B())) outputs?
class Animal: def speak(self): return 'generic'. class Dog(Animal): def speak(self): return 'woof'. def call(a): return a.speak(). What does call(Dog()) return?
